clue.text: Candle holder about to be stuck into cake

indicators.note: something stuck into a thing is pushed inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a scone is a small plain cake
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A candle is stuck into a birthday cake, about to be lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be' reads as a time phrase, but 'about' is the abbreviation C, which goes inside SCONE after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a bracket fixed to a wall that holds candles or lights.

clue.text: Writer's attribute article ignored

indicators.note: a thing ignored is left out, so the named word is dropped

blocks.note: to ascribe something is to attribute it
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A journalist's attribution of a quote leaves out an article.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the article A from the front of ASCRIBE; the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a writer, historically one who copied documents by hand.

clue.text: Almost take place next to principal brought over after duck dish

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter of the verb is cut
brought over suggests being turned over, so the combined letters run the other way

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like O
to occur is to take place
the principal person in charge is the boss

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying a table: a duck dish placed beside the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird the dish is made from, but it is cricket's score of nought. 'Brought over' turns round everything before it, not just the principal.
explanation.definitionFit: Osso buco is an Italian dish of braised veal shanks, here spelt with a double C.

clue.text: Swear remedy must include touch of sun

indicators.note: a touch is just a small bit, so only the opening letter is taken
to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
the first letter of sun

explanation.surface: Advice that any remedy for sunburn should involve a little sunshine, worth swearing about.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear, using bad language.

clue.text: Programme information ringed by girl

indicators.note: a thing ringed by another is encircled, so it sits inside the outer word

blocks.note: Ada is a girl's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A programme leaflet with key information circled by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme or list of items to deal with at a meeting.

clue.text: Crack crackers and become very angry

blocks.note: to have a crack at something is to have a go
crackers and bananas both mean mad

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot open the crackers loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Crack' and 'crackers' look like one idea, but each gives its own piece: a crack is an attempt, and crackers means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bananas is an informal idiom for flying into a rage.

clue.text: Slow-moving shark in harbour

blocks.note: first meaning: a sluggish bottom-dwelling shark of warm seas
second meaning: to keep a feeling in mind, as in a grudge

explanation.surface: A sluggish shark drifting about a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' looks like a place for the shark, but it is a verb, as in harbouring a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: The nurse shark is a slow species, and to nurse a grievance is to harbour it.

clue.text: Reluctant to produce a limerick?

blocks.note: taken as written
a limerick is one example of verse, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to come up with a comic five-line poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that limerick is an example of the wider category of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed to it and so unwilling.

clue.text: Vertical pipe, part of boiler I serviced

indicators.note: part of says the letters are only a section of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of boiler, the I and the start of serviced

explanation.surface: A plumber's report on the upright pipe of a boiler they have serviced.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing, a riser is an upright pipe carrying water or gas between floors.

clue.text: English poet and Scottish one nearly surrounded by pigs

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the name is dropped
a thing surrounded by another sits within it

blocks.note: swine is a word for pigs
Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: Two poets, one English and one Scottish, find themselves among a herd of pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish one' carries on from 'English poet', so it means a Scottish poet; the Scottish word burn for a stream is a tempting but wrong route.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English poet.

clue.text: Conceited dandy led the way

blocks.note: a swell is an old word for a fashionable dandy
to head a group is to lead the way

explanation.surface: A vain fop who strutted at the front of the procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone swell-headed has an inflated opinion of themselves, that is, vanity.

clue.text: Lacking self-control, consuming alcohol to excess

blocks.note: first meaning: unrestrained, immoderate in behaviour
second meaning: given to heavy drinking

explanation.surface: A description of a heavy drinker who cannot hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings run together as if one description; the word covers general immoderation and specifically excessive drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperate means immoderate in general and, more narrowly, given to drink, the opposite of temperance.

clue.text: Anger about British band in part of the US

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the abbreviation

blocks.note: bile is bitterness or anger
B is the abbreviation for British
a belt is a band, as around the waist

explanation.surface: Fury over a British pop group playing somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but here it means a strip worn round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible Belt is the region of the southern US where evangelical Protestantism is strong.

clue.text: Is desperate for massages, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: to knead muscles is to massage them; the silent K drops away in speech

explanation.surface: Someone who badly wants a massage, or so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone needs something, they require it and are in want of it.

clue.text: Greeting shames incompetent fools, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: all twenty-two letters used

explanation.surface: A greeting that embarrasses foolish people, unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The compliments of the season is a set phrase for a seasonal greeting at Christmas.

clue.text: A short journey inside border for a venerable old lady

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the word is lost
inside places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a march is a border region, as in the Welsh Marches
taken as written
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A brief trip across the frontier made for an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A march is an old word for a frontier district, as in the Welsh Marches along the England-Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family, typically an elderly and respected one.

clue.text: Oarsman in races representing country

indicators.note: something that races dashes about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rower competing in regattas for his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Races' looks like the rowing events but is a verb meaning rushes about.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: See 13
Parisian gangster quickly hiding heroin

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: apace means quickly
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A French criminal swiftly concealing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside APACE before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Apache was a name for a violent Paris street gangster around 1900, taken from the Native American people.

clue.text: Girl is first person to be murdered

blocks.note: taken as written
in Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A girl is the first victim in a murder story.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a girl's given name, the Spanish form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Bacteriologist treated tripe

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so its letters are changed around

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A scientist who studied tripe in the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe is cow's stomach lining eaten as food, which is why a bacteriologist might be examining it.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Petri was the German bacteriologist who gave his name to the Petri dish.

clue.text: Left in row for roof worker

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the second

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a quarrel over who will fix the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line or rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays tiles, and roofs are often covered with them.

clue.text: Lazy types exhausted, last in heats

indicators.note: last in points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: dead beat means completely exhausted
the final letter of heats

explanation.surface: Idle runners worn out after finishing at the back in their qualifying races.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadbeats are idle, feckless people who avoid work or debts.

clue.text: Meat embargo hampering small company

indicators.note: hampering suggests closing round and restricting, so the outer word holds the other inside

blocks.note: an embargo is a ban
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A trade embargo on meat crippling a small firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured meat from the back or sides of a pig.

clue.text: Poet in saddle on eastern hilltop

blocks.note: a col is a saddle, a dip between two mountain peaks
E is the abbreviation for eastern
a ridge is the crest of a hill

explanation.surface: A poet sitting in a saddle on a hill in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saddle' suggests riding, but in mountain terms it is a pass between peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was the English Romantic poet who wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Mount Carmel's first section

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of Carmel
a limb is a section or branch, as of a tree or organisation

explanation.surface: The first stretch of Mount Carmel, the ridge in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount Carmel' reads as one name, but Mount is the definition, a verb meaning go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount stairs or a hill is to climb them.

clue.text: Crude fox's burrow at end of spinney

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a fox's den is called an earth
the final letter of spinney

explanation.surface: A rough fox's den at the edge of a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinney is a British word for a small wood or copse.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and unrefined, so crude in that sense.

clue.text: Open out a French bap

blocks.note: un is French for a
a bap is a soft bread roll

explanation.surface: Splitting open a French bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British word for a soft round bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To unroll something is to open it out flat from a rolled state.
